newsitem.title: UK: Eurobond trade ideas - Sell IBRD in lire and marks.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond trade ideas - Sell IBRD in lire and marks.

text.p: Bond analysts' latest trade ideas featured the Eurolire, Eurodollar and Euromark sectors.
** Following are latest trade ideas, compiled by Reuters** EUROLIRE
STRATEGY Over the last month EIB has outperformed KFW by

approximately 40 basis points in price terms. EIB is expensive against the swap and the BTP (trading respectively at 41 and 48 b.p. through). KFW is attractive as it is cheap against the swap at only 7 b.p. through. It offers a pick up in yield of 32 b.p. for a reduction in duration of three months.
STRATEGY This switch has been quite popular among

investors as it allows them to cash in the premium of EIB 10.25 pct to buy the EIB 7.55 pct which is trading close to par. This switch also has the advantage that it offers a pick up in yield of around 13 b.p. and a delayed pay date for the EIB 7.55 pct (ie November 05, 1996)
STRATEGY World Bank is expensive against the swap

(trading at 28 b.p. through) compared to NIB which is cheap (trading at only 12 b.p. through). NIB offers a yield of 20 b.p. for almost the same duration. In addition, both bonds trade on a bid/offer spread of 25 b.p.
STRATEGY Over the last month Eurofima has outperformed

GEC by approximately 80 b.p. in price terms. Eurofima is expensive against the swap and the BTP (trading respectively at 33 and 26 b.p. through) compared to GEC which is cheap (trading respectively at 21 and 10 b.p. through). GEC is attractive as it represents a 10 b.p. pick up in yield for a slightly shorter duration. EURODOLLAR
STRATEGY This switch offers the same credit but extends
the maturity by 7.5 months. The curve is worth 4 b.p. so this beats the curve by 22 b.p. The pick up is at a 5-month historical high of +26 b.p., the average is +19 b.p. and the low is +10b.p.
STRATEGY This move from a supranational to a benchmark

offers a pick up in yield and improved liquidity, whilst shortening the maturity by two months. The yield pick up is at a six-month high of +5 b.p. the average is give-up 7 b.p. and the low is a give-up of 10 b.p.
